title: Investigate sticky throttling caused by shard lease revocation and credit reconciliation gap
creator: Ava Chen
description: Several customers have reported sustained 429s and unexpected billing spikes after shard rebalancing events. Symptoms look like keys that were moved between rate-limiter shards continue to be throttled even after global usage should allow additional tokens. This ticket captures the investigation into shard-level lease revocations, the credit reconciliation gap, and a remediation plan to stop 'sticky' throttles and incorrect accounting.
impact_summary: High: customer-facing 429s for a subset of keys after autoscaling/rebalance events; inaccurate per-key billing leading to billing disputes for 3 enterprise customers and internal spike alarms. Incident rate: ~0.03% of requests in rebalancing windows but hits critical routes for affected customers.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a controlled cluster-scale rebalance on a staging environment with the rate-limiter sharded by org-key.
2) Rapidly send requests for a small set of API keys routed to shard A to exhaust their local burst credits.
3) Trigger lease revocation/transfer of those keys from shard A -> shard B (simulate node restart or autoscale down).
4) Observe that shard B starts serving requests for the keys but does not have synchronized credit state; requests are either allowed incorrectly or rejected for a long time depending on timing.
5) Verify accounting streams (ingest + reconciler logs) to confirm duplicate/dropped credit adjustments and the period where central metering disagrees with shard-local counters.
hypothesis_and_root_cause: Preliminary root cause: during lease revocation the in-memory per-shard token cache is not being atomically reconciled with the central metering snapshot. The transfer sequence currently: revoke lease -> move routing -> shard B boots local cache lazily from central state. If requests arrive in the window before shard B has reconciled the latest debit entries, we observe two problem modes: (a) negative double-charge when both shard A and central reconciler apply debits, and (b) sticky throttle where shard B believes remaining tokens are zero because timid refresh logic ignored in-flight deltas. Contributing factors: non-idempotent delta application, use of wall-clock timers for lease expiration (clock skew between nodes), and lack of versioned credit tokens for safe handoff.
observability_findings: Rate of 429s spikes aligned with container termination events in cluster logs.
Metering stream shows 'missing' debit events for the keys during rebalance windows followed by gap-filling reconciler writes.
KV cache hit ratio drops during transfer, but local throttling decisions continue using stale cached values.
No explicit error traces from central enforcer indicating conflict; race appears at handoff boundary.
proposed_fix: Implement versioned credit handoff plus two-phase lease transfer: (1) pre-transfer snapshot + increment reservation, (2) atomic commit on new owner before serving traffic, and (3) queued replay of in-flight deltas if any are observed. Also add idempotent delta application with sequence numbers attached to every debit/credit event. Short-term patch: force synchronous cache bootstrap on lease acquisition for high-SLA routes (configurable flag) to avoid stale-local decisions.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature-flag guarded code to runtime-1.20 branch and enable in staging for controlled namespaces. 2) Run canary on non-critical orgs for 48h and observe 429s and billing reconciliation metrics. 3) If stable, roll feature flag to 25% prod traffic for low-SLA routes and 100% for critical routes after 7 days. 4) Disable synchronous bootstrap fallback after stable metrics observed for 30 days and finalize removal of the old handoff path in runtime-1.21.
